edition.witness_note: Lake 1912 Loeb copy-text via First1KGreek; second witness (Lightfoot 1889 / Funk) not yet locked. Chapters 1-9 survive in Greek.

source_text: [1] Συνεχάρην ὑμῖν μεγάλως ἐν τῷ κυρίῳ ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστῷ, δεξαμένοις τὰ μιμήματα τῆς ἀληθοῦς ἀγάπης καὶ προπέμψασιν, ὡς ἐπέβαλεν ὑμῖν, τοὺς ἐνειλημένους τοῖς ἁγιοπρεπέσιν δεσμοῖς, ἅτινά ἐστιν διαδήματα τῶν ἀληθῶς ὑπὸ θεοῦ καὶ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν ἐκλελεγμένων: [2] καὶ ὅτι ἡ βεβαία τῆς πίστεως ὑμῶν ῥίζα, ἐξ ἀρχαίων καταγγελλομένη χρόνων, μέχρι νῦν διαμένει καὶ καρποφορεῖ εἰς τὸν κύριον ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν, ὃς ὑπέμεινεν ὑπὲρ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν ἕως θανάτου καταντῆσαι, ὃν ἤγειρεν ὁ θεός, λύσας τὰς ὠδῖνας τοῦ ᾅδου: [3] εἰς ὃν οὐκ ἰδόντες πιστεύετε χαρᾷ ἀνεκλαλήτῳ καὶ δεδοξασμένῃ, εἰς ἣν πολλοὶ ἐπιθυμοῦσιν εἰσελθεῖν, εἰδότες, ὅτι χάριτί ἐστε σεσωσμένοι, οὐκ ἐξ ἔργων, ἀλλὰ θελήματι θεοῦ διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
thought_title: A faith rooted from of old, saved by grace
pass_a_gloss: I rejoiced together with you greatly in our Lord Jesus Christ, because you received the imitations (living copies) of true love and sent them forward on their way, as it fell to you to do: those men wrapped in the chains that befit saints, chains which are the diadems of those truly chosen by God and by our Lord. And I rejoiced that the firm root of your faith, which was proclaimed from ancient times, remains until now and bears fruit to our Lord Jesus Christ, who for our sins endured to the point of reaching death, whom God raised, having loosed the birth-pains of Hades. In him, though you have not seen him, you believe with joy that cannot be spoken and that has been glorified, a joy into which many desire to enter, because you know that you have been saved by grace, not from works, but by the will of God through Jesus Christ.
pass_b_english: I rejoiced with you greatly in our Lord Jesus Christ when you welcomed those living images of true love and sent them on their way, as was right for you to do: men wrapped in chains fit for saints, chains that are the crowns of those truly chosen by God and our Lord.

And I rejoiced that the firm root of your faith, proclaimed from long ago, still holds and still bears fruit for our Lord Jesus Christ. For our sins he endured all the way to death, and God raised him, loosing the pangs of Hades (Acts 2:24). You have not seen him, yet you believe in him with a joy too deep for words and full of glory (1 Peter 1:8), a joy many long to enter, knowing that by grace you have been saved, not by works (Ephesians 2:8–9), but by the will of God through Jesus Christ.

choices.why: the prisoners (Ignatius and companions) embody love; 'imitations' sounds fake in English
royal diadem imagery: chains as coronation
exact echo of Acts 2:24 (Western/LXX-style 'Hades'); keep the image

anf_compare.notes: ANF text is this chapter; the excerpt was mislabeled 'Ignatius, Epistle to Polycarp 1'. It is Polycarp, To the Philippians 1 (newadvent 0136). Attribution corrected.

notes: Re-attributed: Polycarp of Smyrna, To the Philippians 1 (was labeled Ignatius to Polycarp).
'Those wrapped in chains' are Ignatius and his fellow prisoners passing through Philippi (Phil. 9.1, 13.2).
Repair 2026-10-02 per checker a: aorist kept ('I rejoiced'); εἰδότες left as ambiguous as the Greek; added arrival removed.

review.notes: Paragraph [1] checked clause by clause. Συνεχάρην ὑμῖν μεγάλως ἐν τῷ κυρίῳ ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστῷ matches A 'I rejoiced together with you greatly in our Lord Jesus Christ' and B 'I rejoiced with you greatly in our Lord Jesus Christ'. δεξαμένοις τὰ μιμήματα τῆς ἀληθοῦς ἀγάπης καὶ προπέμψασιν, ὡς ἐπέβαλεν ὑμῖν is kept (received/sent forward/as it fell to you; welcomed/sent on their way/as was right). ἅτινά ἐστιν διαδήματα τῶν ἀληθῶς ὑπὸ θεοῦ καὶ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν ἐκλελεγμένων is chains as diadems/crowns of those truly chosen by God and our Lord. ἡ βεβαία τῆς πίστεως ὑμῶν ῥίζα...μέχρι νῦν διαμένει καὶ καρποφορεῖ remains and bears fruit. ὃς ὑπέμεινεν ὑπὲρ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν ἕως θανάτου καταντῆσαι, ὃν ἤγειρεν ὁ θεός, λύσας τὰς ὠδῖνας τοῦ ᾅδου keeps Christ enduring for our sins and God raising and loosing. οὐκ ἰδόντες and οὐκ ἐξ ἔργων are preserved. B citations sit beside the matching clauses (Acts 2:24; 1 Peter 1:8; Ephesians 2:8–9) and are not contradicted by the supplied Greek. Notes disclose re-attribution and the εἰδότες ambiguity. Title names the thought.

Source identity: Greek is Polycarp, To the Philippians 1, matching locus and edition. Completeness: all clauses from [1] covered — joy in reception of imitations of true love, sending forward, chains as diadems of the elect, firm root of faith from ancient times enduring and bearing fruit, Christ’s endurance unto death, resurrection, loosing of Hades’ pangs, unseen belief with inexpressible and glorified joy, many desiring that joy, salvation by grace not works but God’s will through Christ. Negation: 'οὐκ ἐξ ἔργων' rendered as 'not by works' in Pass B and implied in Pass A’s 'not from works'; preserved. Agency: God raises Christ, Christ endures for our sins, believers are saved by God’s will; clear in both. Modality: 'ἐξ ἀρχαίων καταγγελλομένη χρόνων' rendered as 'proclaimed from ancient times' (Pass A) and 'proclaimed from long ago' (Pass B); durative sense preserved. Doctrine: salvation by grace not works, Christ’s resurrection, Hades overcome — all present. Scripture: Pass B cites Acts 2:24 for 'λύσας τὰς ὠδῖνας τοῦ ᾅδου', 1 Peter 1:8 for 'οὐκ ἰδόντες… χαρᾷ ἀνεκλαλήτῳ καὶ δεδοξασμένῃ', Ephesians 2:8–9 for 'χάριτί ἐστε σεσωσμένοι, οὐκ ἐξ ἔργων' — all match wording and are correctly added as required. Title: 'A faith rooted from of old, saved by grace' names the thought (rooted faith, grace salvation), not just locus. Notes disclose OCR-related re-attribution and repair. No uncertainties. All checks pass.
